prompt: The data science team (5 people) at a nationwide parcel delivery company uses logistic regression in a SageMaker notebook to predict whether a delivery will be delayed. About 2 million delivery records accumulate in Amazon S3 each day, and the training data is about 300 million records from the most recent 6 months. The postal code column has about 30,000 unique values. One-hot encoding would expand it to 30,000 columns, which slows training and causes severe sparsity. Label encoding, which converts postal codes to integers in sorted order, gives the values a false ordinal meaning in a linear model. New postal codes appear occasionally, the operations team must be able to explain results by looking at the coefficients, and training time must also be reduced. The team keeps a schedule of retraining once a week. The model coefficients are submitted every quarter to the logistics planning team as explanatory material, and the encoding must be reproducible inside the training pipeline. Additional infrastructure cost cannot increase. Given these constraints, which encoding is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply label encoding as is, assigning integers from 1 to 30,000 to the postal codes in sorted order

choices.label: B
choices.text: Encode the postal code into a single numeric column by using the target mean or the occurrence frequency calculated within the training folds

choices.label: C
choices.text: Calculate the delay rate for each postal code by using the entire dataset and add this value as a new column to both the training and test sets

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leave the postal code column as strings and feed it directly to the model, letting logistic regression handle the categorical values automatically

explanation: Target mean encoding or frequency encoding calculated within the training folds is the correct answer. It uses only one column, so it avoids the explosion in dimensionality, and it does not create an ordinal meaning. Label encoding is the method that the question has already stated is inappropriate. Calculating the delay rate by using the entire dataset causes target leakage, because information about the correct answers in the test set enters the features. If the strings are fed directly, logistic regression accepts only numeric input, so a separate encoding is required.

prompt: An internal document classification model (about 300 MB, able to run inference on a CPU) has been trained and registered in Amazon SageMaker. The model is called irregularly a few times a day, a few requests at a time, from an internal tool used by a handful of HR staff. There are no calls for most of the day. Callers must receive the response in the same request, but a delay of a few seconds on the first request after an idle period does not affect their work. The model is operated by a 3-person development team that has no staff to manage servers, and the team has been told to minimize monthly cost as much as possible. The deployment owner has set a monthly cost limit, and the call volume does not exceed several thousand requests in total for a month. The model is updated only once per quarter. The caller is a web screen on the company portal, so it is acceptable for the response to return within tens of seconds. Which deployment method is the MOST cost-effective without requiring infrastructure management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run a real-time endpoint continuously on two ml.m5.large instances distributed across two Availability Zones and keep them always warm

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an asynchronous inference endpoint, fix the minimum instance count at 1, and queue requests in an S3-based queue for processing

choices.label: C
choices.text: Schedule a batch transform job to run every hour, classify the accumulated documents in bulk regardless of whether any calls were made, and load the results

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deploy to a SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint with the memory set to at least the model size, and accept cold starts

explanation: A serverless inference endpoint is the correct answer. It suits intermittent traffic with long idle periods and tolerable cold starts, it requires no instance selection or scaling policy management, and it scales down to 0 when there are no requests. Memory is usually set to at least the model size. Two always-running instances incur cost even during hours with no calls. An asynchronous endpoint fixed at a minimum of 1 instance also incurs cost at all times and does not return the response immediately. An hourly batch job does not meet the requirement to respond immediately to each call.

prompt: A used-car price prediction team tunes XGBoost with SageMaker automatic model tuning. The team specified the eta range as 0.0001 to 1.0 and searched with a linear scale, and most of the values tried were concentrated in the 0.1 to 1.0 range, so the small learning rate region was barely explored. The learning rate has an effect across several orders of magnitude, so the entire range must be explored evenly. The training job budget is fixed at 30 jobs that have already been approved and cannot be increased. The search covers two hyperparameters, eta and max_depth, and the objective metric is validation RMSE. The existing training script and data will not be changed. The training data used for the search is about 800,000 rows, and each job finishes within a few minutes. The team manages the tuning job by defining it in SDK code to keep it reproducible. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Narrow the range to 0.1 to 1.0 to increase search density, and exclude the small learning rate region from the search

choices.label: B
choices.text: Specify the ScalingType of that continuous hyperparameter as Logarithmic and search on a log scale

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specify the ScalingType as ReverseLogarithmic to search more densely for values close to 1.0

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the search strategy to Random, because values are then sampled uniformly across orders of magnitude and no scale needs to be specified

explanation: A positive range that spans several orders of magnitude should be searched on a Logarithmic scale so that each order of magnitude is sampled at a similar rate. With a linear scale, about 90% of the budget is spent on the 0.1 to 1.0 range. Narrowing the range prevents exploration of small learning rates and violates the requirement. ReverseLogarithmic is intended for ranges that are sensitive to values close to 1.0, so it works in the opposite direction from what the question needs. The Random strategy is independent of how the scale is specified, and if the ScalingType is linear, the same concentration occurs.

prompt: An online fashion store team is training a multi-label classification model that assigns several attributes, such as 'casual', 'summer', and 'cotton', to clothing images at the same time. The team uses the SageMaker built-in image classification algorithm with an augmented manifest (Pipe mode). The labels come from a manifest created by another department's system, and the class value is a list of the relevant class IDs, such as '[0, 2]', with num_classes set to 3. This manifest is a shared file that another team updates every day, so it cannot be modified on our side, but when training is run, the labels are interpreted differently from what is expected. There is no problem with the training instance or the image location. There are about 400,000 images, and the team wants to adjust only the settings in the training job definition without changing the training script or container. What is the MOST appropriate solution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Specify the content type as 'application/x-recordio; label-format=class-id' so that the labels are interpreted as a list of class IDs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reduce num_classes to 2 to match the maximum length of the class ID list

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change RecordWrapperType to None so that the manifest is read in the original image format

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the class values in the manifest to multi-hot vectors such as '[1, 0, 1]', leave the content type at its default, re-upload the manifest file, and ask the other team that shares it to use the new format as well

explanation: Multi-label training for image classification accepts labels in two formats, multi-hot vectors (the default) or a list of class IDs. Because the default is multi-hot, the class ID format must be interpreted correctly by explicitly specifying label-format=class-id in the content type. Because the manifest cannot be modified, setting the content type is the solution. Converting to multi-hot requires modifying the data, which violates the constraint. num_classes is the total number of classes, so 3 is correct. For an augmented manifest, RecordWrapperType must be set to RecordIO.

prompt: A recommendation data team at an e-commerce company predicts purchase conversion by using the SageMaker built-in XGBoost algorithm. The training AUC is 0.99 but the validation AUC is 0.86, and the gap widens as num_round is increased. The current max_depth is 12, early_stopping_rounds is not set, and lambda and alpha are at their default values. Training uses a single ml.m5.4xlarge instance and one training run takes about 40 minutes. No additional data can be collected this quarter, and the feature set has already been finalized and cannot be changed. The validation set is a separate sample from the same period as the training data, and leakage has already been checked. The training pipeline is defined as a SageMaker training job and can be rerun by changing only the hyperparameters. Which actions MOST effectively reduce overfitting? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Double num_round to build more trees and train for longer so that validation performance catches up

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower min_child_weight to 0 so that leaves with few samples are also allowed to split and the model learns in finer detail

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lower max_depth to around 6 to reduce the complexity of each individual tree

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set lambda and alpha to 0 to remove the regularization terms so that the model can fit the data more flexibly

choices.label: E
choices.text: Set early_stopping_rounds so that training stops if the validation metric does not improve for a given number of rounds

explanation: Increasing max_depth makes the model more complex and prone to overfitting, so lowering it from 12 to about 6 reduces the capacity of each tree. early_stopping_rounds stops training when the validation score no longer improves and uses the best model, which prevents the gap from widening as the number of rounds increases. Increasing num_round makes overfitting worse. The larger the values of lambda and alpha, the more conservative the model becomes, so setting them to 0 removes regularization. A larger min_child_weight is more conservative, so lowering it to 0 moves in the direction of overfitting.

prompt: Several teams at a financial holding company store source data for training in 120 Amazon S3 buckets. Under company regulations, objects that contain sensitive information such as credit card numbers and email addresses must be identified before they are used for training, and the object formats vary, including CSV, JSON, and logs. New objects are continually added to the buckets, and the security team (4 people) wants to receive the results in a regular report. Moving data is not allowed, so objects cannot be copied to another location for analysis, and the security team has no capacity to develop scanning code. All of the target buckets are in a single AWS account and Region, the results are compiled into the security team's regular report once a week, and real-time alerts for each finding are not required. Which approach MOST appropriately meets these requirements without writing or operating scanning code?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Write a scanner that reads all objects and finds patterns by using regular expressions in an AWS Lambda function, and run it periodically with Amazon EventBridge

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run an Amazon Macie sensitive data discovery job on the target buckets and review the findings produced by managed data identifiers

choices.label: C
choices.text: Query the object metadata in S3 Inventory reports with Amazon Athena to determine whether sensitive information is included

choices.label: D
choices.text: Turn on the S3 protection feature of Amazon GuardDuty to detect objects that contain sensitive information

explanation: Macie finds sensitive data such as credit card numbers and email addresses in S3 objects by using managed data identifiers based on machine learning and pattern matching, and it reports findings through discovery jobs for which you specify the target buckets and scope, so it meets the requirements without code. A Lambda scanner violates the constraint that it must not be written and operated by the team. Inventory metadata does not contain the contents of objects, so it cannot be used to determine whether sensitive information is present. GuardDuty is a service that detects threats and anomalous activity; it does not classify sensitive data in object contents.

prompt: An online marketplace collects purchase events for a real-time recommendation pipeline in a single account and Region. Three consumers, a fraud detection service, a recommendation feature computation, and an audit archive, must each read the same events independently, and when a failure occurs, they must be able to reread the last 24 hours of data for reprocessing. Two or three more consumers may be added in the future. Each event is about 2 KB, 5,000 events arrive per second, and it is sufficient to preserve event order only per user ID. There are only 2 data engineers, so they prefer a managed service with a small operational burden. The events contain no personally identifiable information, so there are no retention restrictions. Reprocessing is rare and happens only during failures, and the audit archive consumer stores events separately for 1 year. Which ingestion layer MOST appropriately meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Put the events into a single Amazon SQS standard queue and have the three consumers share and read messages from the same queue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Publish the events to an Amazon SNS topic and subscribe an HTTP endpoint for each consumer to receive them by push

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ingest into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and have each consumer run as an independent application that reads the records within the retention period on its own

choices.label: D
choices.text: Store the events in Amazon S3 through a Firehose delivery stream, create a separate bucket for each consumer, and have each consumer read and process the files whenever an S3 object event arrives

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams retains records for the retention period (24 hours by default, up to 365 days), and multiple applications can read from one stream independently and concurrently, so it meets the requirements for reprocessing and consumer expansion. In an SQS standard queue, one message is processed and deleted by one consumer, so the three consumers cannot all read the same event. SNS delivers by push, so rereading for reprocessing is not possible. The combination of Firehose and S3 has buffering delay and is not a real-time consumption model.

prompt: The demand forecasting team at a large supermarket chain builds a daily sales regression model with Amazon SageMaker. The sales data contains extreme values, up to 20 times normal levels, caused by a few large promotions each year. These are real, normal sales, so they are not removed. The business team wants to understand 'how many units we are off by on average' in the same units as sales volume, and does not want a few extreme values to dominate the metric. Forecasts are generated by a batch job every morning, and only one metric appears in the management report. Three candidate models are compared on the same validation set. The management report is read by executives with no statistical background, and the ranking among the candidate models must not flip because of a few outliers. The model is trained on 3 years of daily historical data, and the last 2 months are used for validation. Which metric is MOST appropriate for comparing the models?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Root mean squared error (RMSE), the value obtained by squaring the errors and taking the square root to convert back to sales volume units

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mean squared error (MSE), the value that puts greater weight on large errors and strongly reflects failures to predict extreme values

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mean absolute error (MAE), the mean of the absolute values of the errors, interpreted in the same units as sales volume

choices.label: D
choices.text: Coefficient of determination (R²), the proportion of variance explained by the model, expressed as a unitless value

explanation: MAE is the mean of the absolute values of the errors, so it can be interpreted in the same units as sales volume, and because it does not square the errors, a few extreme values dominate the metric less. RMSE also has the same units, but it squares the errors, so it is pulled strongly by extreme values. MSE has squared units, which makes it hard to interpret, and it is even more sensitive to extreme values. R² is unitless and does not tell you how many units you are off by on average. Therefore, MAE is the metric that meets both requirements: interpretable units and insensitivity to extreme values.

prompt: A logistics data team wants to convert 1.5 TB of logs stored in Amazon S3 as gzip CSV into a columnar format just once, to reduce later Amazon Athena query costs. The team is familiar with SQL, does not want to operate a new cluster or servers, and the conversion is a one-time task. The source logs are organized by daily prefixes, and the monthly Athena query volume is tens of terabytes. The original data must be preserved as is after conversion for audit purposes, and the converted output is placed under a different S3 prefix in the same Region. The work must be finished within three days before the quarter close. The converted output is used by monthly reporting queries and dashboards, and the queries mainly read date ranges and a few columns. There is only one data engineer. Which method is the MOST cost-effective and has the LEAST operational overhead while meeting these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an Amazon EMR cluster, convert with a Spark job, and keep the cluster running so it can also be used for later conversions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run an AWS Glue crawler to create a table, and the crawler automatically rewrites the S3 objects as Parquet

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use an Athena CTAS query to read the source table and store a new table converted to Parquet format in Amazon S3

choices.label: D
choices.text: Read the files one by one with pandas on a SageMaker notebook instance, save them as Parquet, upload them again, and keep the instance running after the conversion

explanation: An Athena CTAS query stores query results as a new table in a columnar format such as Parquet in one step, so the one-time conversion can be completed with SQL alone and without servers. When partitioning, a CTAS query has a limit of 100 partitions per query, so the work must be split and run with INSERT INTO. Keeping an EMR cluster running costs more and has a greater operational burden than a one-time job requires. A crawler only registers the schema in the catalog and does not convert the data files. Processing 1.5 TB with pandas on a single notebook has memory and time limits and requires a lot of manual work.

prompt: The ML team at a streaming service wants to automatically scale the number of instances up and down on a real-time endpoint whose traffic varies greatly between day and night. The endpoint has one production variant called Variant1 and uses ml.c5.xlarge instances. Traffic differs greatly, with hundreds of requests per second during the day and only a few per second at night. Cost reduction is needed, but response latency must also be maintained, and deleting and recreating the endpoint is not allowed because it would interrupt service. With limited operations staff, the team does not want to maintain a custom-built scheduler. The variant starts with 2 instances and must keep at least 1 instance even at night. The team wants to base scaling on the number of invocations per instance. Which two steps are required to configure auto scaling that meets these requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run a Lambda function every 5 minutes with Amazon EventBridge that creates a new endpoint configuration each time to change the instance count

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group for each instance type directly and add the SageMaker endpoint instances to the group

choices.label: C
choices.text: Auto scaling can be used only with a serverless endpoint, so first change to a serverless endpoint

choices.label: D
choices.text: Register the variant as a scalable target of Application Auto Scaling by specifying the endpoint name and the variant name

choices.label: E
choices.text: Define a scaling policy such as target tracking and apply it to the registered scalable target so that the instance count is adjusted

explanation: The correct steps are registering the variant as a scalable target and defining and applying a scaling policy. The flow in the documentation is to register the model variant as a scalable target (the endpoint name and variant name are required), and then to define and apply a policy. Swapping endpoint configurations with Lambda creates a large operational burden because you build it yourself. An instance-based real-time endpoint cannot be converted to serverless, and there is no need to do so. Managed endpoint instances cannot be added to an EC2 Auto Scaling group.

prompt: The demand forecasting team at a retailer trains a model on 2 years of daily sales data to forecast next week's demand. The team randomly shuffled all rows and used 80% for training and 20% for validation. The validation error was very low, but after deployment the actual error increased significantly. There are 1,200 products, seasonality and promotion effects are pronounced, and the forecasts are used to decide order quantities every Friday. The model also uses lag features such as the previous week's sales, and the data has already been cleaned, so no additional collection is needed. There are no new products and only the existing 1,200 are handled, and the evaluation metric is WAPE. The team monitors the post-deployment error on a monthly basis. Orders are placed per product but only once a week. How should the validation set be constructed to estimate performance MOST realistically under production conditions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sample randomly stratified by day of the week, keep the current setup in which data from the same week is mixed between training and validation, and calculate the evaluation metric as mean absolute error

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase the size of the validation set to 40% of the total and report the average error obtained by repeating the random split several times as the performance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use only the dates with the highest sales volume as the validation set to confirm that the model performs well even in the worst case

choices.label: D
choices.text: Preserve the time order, train on an earlier period, and use the most recent period after it as the validation set so that the model predicts the future

explanation: A split that respects time order is the correct answer. After deployment the model always predicts the future beyond the training period, so validation should also use a period after the training period to be realistic. With a random split, values from adjacent dates are mixed into both sides and the model effectively sees future information, so the error comes out low. Stratifying by day of the week or repeating random splits has the same problem and only changes the size. Choosing only days with high sales biases the distribution and does not represent overall performance.

prompt: The demand forecasting team at a delivery platform wants to include an 'order time (0 to 23 hours)' feature in its model. The team uses a distance-based algorithm and a neural network, and if the hour is used as an integer, 23:00 and 0:00 become values that are very far apart, so the fact that they are adjacent times of day is not reflected. In addition to order time, the model uses numeric features such as day of the week, rainfall, and distance, and the training data is 8 million records. As the number of features increases, training time increases proportionally, and the current training time is already close to the limit of the overnight batch window. The encoding must be computed once in SageMaker Processing and applied in the same way to training and inference. The team does not use a separate trainable embedding layer. Which encoding preserves the cyclical nature of time BEST while adding the fewest columns?

choices.label: A
choices.text: One-hot encode each of the 24 hour values, creating an independent binary column for each time slot, and feed them to the model

choices.label: B
choices.text: Standardize the hour to a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1 to reduce the range of values, and use it as is in the same single column

choices.label: C
choices.text: Transform the hour into two columns, sine and cosine, so that 23:00 and 0:00 are represented as close points on a circle

choices.label: D
choices.text: Divide the hour into only two categories, AM and PM, convert it into a single binary column, and discard the detailed time information

explanation: The sine and cosine transformation is the correct answer. It maps the hour to a point on a circle so that 23:00 and 0:00 are close, and only two columns are added. One-hot encoding increases the columns to 24 and loses the similarity of adjacent time slots. Standardization only changes the range of values, and the distance between 23 and 0 remains large. AM/PM binarization uses few columns but loses most of the detailed information, such as differences in demand by time slot.

prompt: A card company's fraud detection team trained a model in Amazon SageMaker. Evaluated on the test set with a threshold of 0.5, it shows accuracy of 99.6% and ROC AUC of 0.96. The fraud rate in the test set is 0.3%, and of the 1,200 actual fraudulent transactions, the model caught only 300. Management says that the accuracy is high so the model should be deployed, and wants to put the accuracy figure in the month-end report as is. The team, on the other hand, believes that the cost of missing fraud is high, and the operations team is concerned that more false positives will lead to more customer inquiries. The model is retrained once a month, and this evaluation result is an agenda item for the model approval meeting next week. The average loss when a single fraud is missed is much greater than the handling cost of one false positive. Which metrics should be checked together FIRST to judge model quality?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The overall accuracy recalculated after increasing the size of the test set, and the value displayed to more decimal places

choices.label: B
choices.text: Recall (here 25%) and precision, and PR AUC, the area under the precision-recall curve

choices.label: C
choices.text: A learning curve that shows whether the loss on the training data decreased at every epoch

choices.label: D
choices.text: The specificity alone, the proportion of normal transactions correctly classified as normal

explanation: With imbalanced data in which positives are only 0.3%, accuracy comes out at nearly 99.7% even if every transaction is predicted as normal, so accuracy cannot reveal quality. Here recall is 300/1,200, or 25%, so 75% of fraud is being missed, which means recall and precision must be examined together with PR AUC, which is sensitive to the minority class. Increasing the test size does not remove the limitation of accuracy. A learning curve does not show generalization performance. Specificity is a metric for the majority normal class and cannot reveal the missed fraud.

prompt: A marketing analytics team trained the SageMaker built-in XGBoost algorithm on a CSV file exported from Athena (with a header row and the target column as the last column), specifying text/csv for the train channel. The results are meaningless and the validation metrics are abnormal. The training job uses the text/csv content type, the data is in the train prefix in Amazon S3, and the source of 30 million rows is re-exported every day by an Athena query. The training job definition and channel configuration are already approved and will not be changed. XGBoost training runs on a single ml.m5.2xlarge instance, and the validation channel is also stored in a separate prefix in the same way. The export query runs automatically every day in Athena. Which is the MOST appropriate way to resolve the problem with the MINIMUM change when regenerating the training data?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Leave the target column as the last column and add label_size=1 to the content type so that the last column is read as the label

choices.label: B
choices.text: The algorithm automatically skips the header row, so just change the channel name to validation and train again

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the content type to application/json, leave the CSV file as is, and let the algorithm infer the format

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remove the header row, move the target column to be the first column, resave the CSV, and specify it as text/csv

explanation: For CSV training input to SageMaker built-in algorithms, there must be no header row and the target variable must be in the first column, so deleting the header and moving the target column to the front is the minimum change. The setting that reads the last column as the label differs from this rule, and label_size is a value that specifies the number of label columns. The header is not skipped automatically, and the training channel name must be train. Simply changing the content type to JSON does not cause a CSV file to be interpreted.

prompt: For a text classification neural network that a review analysis team trains in Amazon SageMaker, the training loss keeps decreasing through epoch 30, but the validation loss starts to increase after epoch 9. The model is trained on 50,000 English reviews, and the labeling budget is exhausted, so no more data can be collected. The evaluation metrics are validation accuracy and validation loss, and because changing the architecture would deviate from the already approved design, the number of hidden layers and the number of units per layer are left unchanged. Training runs on a single ml.p3.2xlarge instance and takes several minutes per epoch, so reducing unnecessary epochs also reduces cost. There is no budget to run an additional hyperparameter search this week, and the team must change one or two things in the current settings and retrain. The validation set has 5,000 records, and its class distribution is the same as that of the training set. Which actions appropriately improve generalization performance? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Merge the validation set into the training set and stop monitoring the validation loss to increase the training data

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase the number of epochs to 100 and continue training while waiting for the validation loss to come back down

choices.label: C
choices.text: Apply early stopping, which stops training when the validation loss does not improve, and use the model from around epoch 9

choices.label: D
choices.text: Apply dropout to the outputs of the existing hidden layers and add weight decay (L2 regularization) to suppress overfitting

choices.label: E
choices.text: Greatly increase the number of hidden layers and units to enlarge model capacity, which should also bring the validation loss down

explanation: The point at which the validation loss starts to rise is a sign of overfitting, so using early stopping to take the model at the point of best validation performance, and using dropout and L2 regularization to reduce how much the model memorizes the training data, improves generalization while keeping the number of layers and units the same. Increasing capacity makes overfitting worse, and increasing epochs widens the gap. If the validation set is merged into training and monitoring is cut off, there is no way to detect overfitting, and it also becomes impossible to estimate generalization performance.

prompt: A clothing store team builds a return prediction model. The 'size' column has six values, XS, S, M, L, XL, and XXL, and the size order is meaningful. There are 250,000 samples and the data has already been cleaned. The model is from the regression family, and the team plans to keep using it in order to obtain easily interpretable coefficients. Several other categorical columns have already been one-hot encoded, bringing the number of columns above 400, and adding more would hit the memory limit of the training pipeline. The size values are already normalized with no typos. The model coefficient is used to report how much the return probability changes when the size goes up by one step. The handling of the size column must be changeable in a single line in a notebook, and no additional packages will be used. What is the SIMPLEST way to represent the size in a single column while preserving the order information?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply ordinal encoding that maps the sizes to integers in size order, from XS=1 to XXL=6, and represent them in a single column

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply one-hot encoding that creates a binary column for each of the six values, completely removing any assumption about order, and estimate a separate regression coefficient for each size value

choices.label: C
choices.text: Apply label encoding that assigns integers after sorting alphabetically, and leave it to the model to learn the order on its own

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use the number of characters in the size string as a new numeric column, converting so that one-character values and values of two or more characters are distinguished

explanation: Ordinal encoding that maps integers in size order is the correct answer. It preserves the size order in a single column, so it respects the constraint that the number of columns must not increase, and it is easy to interpret with a single regression coefficient. However, it is a simplification that assumes the gaps between adjacent sizes are equal. One-hot encoding increases the columns to six and loses the order information. Label encoding in alphabetical order creates an order that differs from the actual sizes, such as L, M, S, XL, and gives the wrong meaning. The number of characters cannot distinguish M from S and is unrelated to size.

prompt: An online shopping company forecasts daily demand for about 6,000 products up to 28 days ahead. The products show similar seasonal patterns, and new products are added every week with short histories. Whether there is a promotion (0/1) is known in advance for the future period, and product category information is also available. The forecasts are delivered to the inventory system every morning, and only two people manage the models, so they cannot train, deploy, and monitor a separate model for each product. The company already uses Amazon SageMaker and the data is in Amazon S3. Forecast accuracy is evaluated with WAPE, and new products have less than 2 weeks of history. The forecasts must arrive in Amazon S3 by 6 AM every morning. It is acceptable if the forecast for a new product's first 4 weeks is not very different from the category average. Which configuration MOST appropriately meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Train a separate ARIMA model for each product and withhold forecasts for new products until enough history accumulates, with the number of models growing as the number of products grows

choices.label: B
choices.text: Train all of the time series in a single DeepAR model, and provide the category as cat and the promotion as dynamic_feat

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obtain anomaly scores for the demand time series with Random Cut Forest and use the average score as the demand estimate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Feed day of the week and product ID one-hot encoded into a Linear Learner regression to directly predict the value 28 days ahead

explanation: DeepAR trains many related time series together in a single RNN model and can also be applied to similar new time series, which is advantageous for new products with short histories, and the documentation explains that with hundreds or more related time series it is better than ARIMA or ETS. For cat you must provide the categories seen during training, and for dynamic_feat you must provide the promotion values, including those for the length of the forecast horizon. ARIMA forces you to manage a separate model for each product. Random Cut Forest is for anomaly detection. Linear Learner does not model time series structure.

prompt: A data scientist on a financial data team standardized the numeric features of 300,000 customer records and replaced missing values with the mean, and then split the result 80:20 into a training set and a test set. The test performance was high, but the performance on newly arriving data was low. Preprocessing and training are already running in production as a monthly batch pipeline consisting of a SageMaker Processing step and a training job, so changes to the structure must be small. The model review meeting is in two days, so a simple fix is needed. The preprocessing code is in one place, the Processing step, and the training step reads its output. New data arrives all at once at the beginning of the month. The evaluation metric is AUC, and the comparison target is the model deployed last month. What should be done to improve the reliability of the evaluation while minimizing changes to the pipeline?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Calculate the mean and standard deviation separately on the test set and standardize only the test set using its own reference so that the distributions match each other

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove the standardization step entirely and use the raw values as is, eliminating all preprocessing steps from the pipeline

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keep the statistics calculated from the entire dataset and change only the split ratio to 70:30 to make the test set larger

choices.label: D
choices.text: First split into training and test sets, calculate the mean and standard deviation only on the training set, and apply the transformation to both sets with the same values

explanation: The correct answer is to split first, calculate the mean, standard deviation, and imputation values only on the training set, and apply the same values to the test set. In the existing order, information from the test set is mixed into the statistics, so the evaluation turns out optimistic. If the test set is standardized with its own statistics, the reference differs from the one used during training, and the model receives a transformation it has never seen. Removing all preprocessing can degrade training quality because of differences in scale. Changing only the split ratio leaves the leakage at the point where the statistics are calculated.

prompt: A medical AI startup runs Amazon SageMaker training jobs on hospital data. The code in the training container (including open-source libraries) must not be able to send data externally, and for this the container must not be able to make outbound calls to any service, including S3, let alone the internet. SageMaker must handle downloading the training data and uploading the results on its behalf. The data is encrypted in Amazon S3 with AWS KMS, and in the security review, training code that uses untrusted third-party packages was pointed out as a risk. Training runs once a month, and the security team requires a technical control that does not rely on code review. The training instance is an ml.p3.2xlarge, and the pretrained weights are included in the container image. SageMaker uploads the resulting artifacts to Amazon S3. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Place the training job in a VPC, block only the internet in the outbound rules of the security group, and allow the S3 gateway endpoint

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set EnableNetworkIsolation to True when creating the training job to block all outbound network calls from the container

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove S3 access permissions from the execution role so that the container cannot access S3, and download the data from a user's PC

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only perform strict code reviews to remove all network calls of the requests library from the training container code, and obtain security team approval before installing third-party packages

explanation: The network isolation setting is the correct answer. When it is enabled, the training and inference containers cannot make outbound calls to any service, including S3, and no credentials are provided; the downloading and uploading of data is handled by SageMaker outside the container by using the execution role. If an S3 endpoint is allowed in the VPC, the container can send data to S3, which violates the requirement. If the S3 permissions are removed from the execution role, SageMaker's downloads and uploads also fail. Code review alone cannot technically block calls from external libraries.

prompt: The ML team at a fintech company wants to deploy a newly trained model as a real-time endpoint. The latency target is a p95 of 100 ms or less, and there are several candidate instance types available. The team wants to use load testing to determine which instance type and count give the best performance for the cost, but wants to minimize the operational burden of building its own benchmark scripts. The model is already registered in Amazon SageMaker, and real-time traffic is concentrated in the morning hours of the day. The decision must be made within two days before deployment, and no one on the team has operated load testing tools before. The candidates are three types, ml.c5.xlarge, ml.m5.2xlarge, and ml.g4dn.xlarge, and the load tests are performed in a development account rather than the production account. The final choice will be based on hourly cost. What is the MOST appropriate method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an endpoint for each candidate instance, run a self-built load generator with Lambda, manually aggregate the metrics, compare them in a spreadsheet, and select the configuration with the lowest latency

choices.label: B
choices.text: Register the model with SageMaker Inference Recommender, run load test jobs for each instance type, and compare the performance and cost metrics

choices.label: C
choices.text: Select the largest GPU instance, check whether it meets the latency target, and evaluate cost after deployment by looking at the bill

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use the recommendation feature on the Savings Plans purchase screen to get recommended instance types and counts that match the model's characteristics, and apply them

explanation: Inference Recommender is the correct answer. You register the model and it automatically runs load tests for each instance type and compares performance and resource utilization metrics, and you pay only for the instances used while the job is running. A self-built load generator creates a large operational burden for scripting and aggregation. Choosing the largest GPU results in using excessive specifications without any comparison of performance against cost. Savings Plans is a commitment discount product and is not an instance recommendation tool based on model performance.

prompt: You are reviewing the preprocessing notebooks for a credit card company's credit scoring model. The goal is to predict, at the time of loan approval, whether a delinquency will occur within 12 months after approval. Three data scientists worked in separate notebooks, and the evaluation results are reported to the risk management committee, which decides whether to approve the model. The notebooks contain all 120 columns and many preprocessing operations, and there is only one day for the review. The evaluation is reported as the AUC on a holdout test set, and whether an operation is leakage is judged by whether that information would be known at prediction time. The data is 400,000 loans from the last 5 years, and the notebooks are version controlled with Git so the change history can be submitted to the committee. Select the two operations that cause data leakage that distorts the model evaluation optimistically and that should be fixed first. (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Split into a training set and a test set by using a stratified split that preserves the class ratio

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fill the missing values with the mean of the entire dataset and then split into a training set and a test set

choices.label: C
choices.text: Include as a model input feature a column that aggregates the number of delinquencies during the 12 months after approval

choices.label: D
choices.text: Calculate an average balance feature by using only the transaction history from the 6 months before the time of approval and use it as input

choices.label: E
choices.text: Standardize the test set in the same way by using the mean and standard deviation calculated on the training set

explanation: Splitting after filling with a mean calculated from the entire dataset, and putting the post-approval delinquency count column into the features, both cause leakage. In the former, information from the test set is mixed into the imputation value, and in the latter, information from the period in which the correct answer is determined is used as a feature, so it cannot be obtained at production time. Applying statistics from the training set to the test set is the correct procedure. Using only transactions before approval is information that is known at prediction time. A stratified split only preserves the class ratio.

prompt: A telecom marketing data team calculates scores for 50 million customer records at 2 AM every day and stores them in Amazon S3. The marketing team uses the results the next morning, and real-time responses for each record are not required. No compute cost should be incurred once the score calculation is finished, and the team wants the input records and the predictions in the same output. The input is organized by date in Amazon S3, intermediate processing results are not needed, and a day that fails may be rerun the next day. The model is already registered in Amazon SageMaker, and there is only one operator. The input is about 30 GB and the model is the SageMaker built-in XGBoost. After the job completes, a downstream AWS Glue job reads the results, and failure notifications are received through Amazon CloudWatch alarms. It is sufficient to store scores to four decimal places. Which approach is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run a real-time endpoint continuously, and have a client on Amazon EC2 call it sequentially for 50 million records and write the responses directly to Amazon S3

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a serverless inference endpoint, raise the concurrency to the maximum, call it in parallel for 50 million records, and collect the responses

choices.label: C
choices.text: Run a SageMaker batch transform job on a schedule and use the setting that joins the input records with the prediction results

choices.label: D
choices.text: Load multiple copies of the same model onto a multi-model endpoint and configure each model to process a share of the data

explanation: Batch transform is the correct answer. It is used for large-scale inference that does not need a persistent endpoint, the instances shut down when the job ends so cost stops, and it has a feature that joins and outputs the input records with the inference results. A real-time endpoint incurs cost throughout the day and requires separate calling code. Serverless is not suited to a batch of 50 million records because of concurrency and per-invocation limits. Loading multiple copies of the same model onto a multi-model endpoint has a different purpose and also does not distribute the processing.

prompt: A consumer goods company's demand planning team validated a model by randomly splitting 36 months of monthly data 80 to 20, and the validation RMSE was low, but the actual error increased significantly after deployment. The model uses the previous month's sales and a moving average as features and is used to forecast demand for the next 3 months, and the data has annual seasonality and a gentle upward trend. The validation results will be used as material for approving capital investment, so a reliable error estimate is needed. The data covers only 36 months, so the period available for training is also limited. There are two candidate models, and errors are compared with RMSE. The team prefers a method that is simple to implement, but the honesty of the validation takes priority. The upward trend and seasonality are both reflected in the features. Which validation method is MOST appropriate for estimating performance under the same conditions as the deployment environment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Repeat the same random split 10 times and average the validation RMSE to reduce the effect of chance in the split

choices.label: B
choices.text: Perform stratified k-fold by month so that all months are evenly included in each fold, and report the average RMSE across folds

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use walk-forward (expanding window) cross-validation that preserves time order, always training on the past and evaluating on the following period

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the validation ratio to 50% to reduce the effect of training data bias and evaluate only once

explanation: In time series, a random split mixes information from future time points into training, and because of lag features such as the previous month's value, validation samples are directly connected to training samples, so performance is overestimated. Walk-forward validation, which preserves time order, always trains on the past and evaluates the period after it, reproducing the deployment conditions. Repeating the random split and stratified k-fold by month both fail to remove the leakage of future information. Increasing the validation ratio leaves the violation of time order unchanged.

prompt: A computer vision team optimizes an image classification CNN with SageMaker automatic model tuning. Each training job emits the validation accuracy as a metric at every epoch, and a single job takes several hours on a GPU. The team wants to stop configurations with poor intermediate results early and reallocate those resources to promising configurations while using many parallel training jobs. The tuning budget is 200 training jobs, and up to 20 can run at the same time. The hyperparameters being tuned are the learning rate (continuous), the batch size, and the dropout rate. The team does not use Spot training and trains on On-Demand GPU instances, and it emits the validation accuracy to Amazon CloudWatch at every epoch. The tuning must be completed within this quarter. Which tuning strategy MOST appropriately meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Select the Hyperband strategy and leave TrainingJobEarlyStoppingType set to OFF to use its internal early stopping feature

choices.label: B
choices.text: Select the grid search strategy, specify the learning rate range as a continuous interval, try all combinations, and then compare the final accuracy of all configurations based on the same number of epochs

choices.label: C
choices.text: Select the random search strategy, run all training jobs to completion, and compare only the final results

choices.label: D
choices.text: Select the Bayesian optimization strategy and limit the number of parallel training jobs to 1 so that previous results are reflected each time

explanation: Hyperband is a multi-fidelity strategy that uses both intermediate and final training results to reallocate epochs to promising configurations, automatically stops poorly performing configurations, and scales to many parallel jobs; when using its internal early stopping, TrainingJobEarlyStoppingType is left OFF. Grid search supports only categorical values, so it cannot be used for a continuous learning rate range. Random search does not reallocate resources based on intermediate results. Limiting parallel jobs to 1 is the opposite of the requirement to use many parallel jobs.

prompt: The rate-setting team at a health insurance company predicts claim risk using the policyholder's 'number of hospital visits in the last year' column. 18% of the 400,000 people have no value in this column. Analysis shows that the customers with missing values are those who did not submit health checkup history, and the fact of being missing is itself correlated with claim risk. The claim risk score is used to calculate insurance premiums, so approaches that arbitrarily exclude some customers or discard information are not acceptable. Missing values occur at the same rate in production. The model is logistic regression, which cannot handle missing values on its own, and because it is used for premium calculation, the basis for each customer's score must be explainable in an audit. Columns with imputed values must be indicated separately in the results documentation. Which method handles the missing values with the LEAST loss of information?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delete all of the 18% of rows with missing values, and train and even evaluate the model with only the customers whose values are filled in

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fill the missing values with 0 and do not create an indicator column, treating them the same as customers who actually had 0 visits, and train

choices.label: C
choices.text: Impute with the median, and also add a binary indicator column showing whether the value was missing so that the model can use the missingness pattern

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exclude this column entirely from the features so that no handling of missing values is needed, and train the model with only the remaining columns

explanation: Using an imputed value together with a missingness indicator column is the correct answer. Because the missingness itself is information, you must fill in the value while also keeping the fact that it was missing in a separate column, so that no information is lost. Deleting the rows loses 18% of the customers and their risk signal altogether, and the distribution also differs from the production data. If you only fill with 0 and do not create an indicator column, it cannot be distinguished from actual 0 visits. Excluding the column discards all of the predictive information in the missingness pattern.

prompt: A data science team at a telecom company is building a subscriber churn prediction model. The training data has a 'number of cancellation consultation calls' column, and because this value is an item recorded by the agent after the customer applies for cancellation, it is filled in only after cancellation. The validation accuracy is very high at 99%, but performance is expected to drop significantly in real operation. This score is used by the marketing team every Monday to select recipients of churn prevention coupons, and the training data is 400,000 subscribers over the past 2 years. The model structure has already been approved and deployment is scheduled for next week. In addition to the cancellation consultation column, there is plenty of information available at the time of subscription, such as plan, tenure, and monthly usage. The marketing team sends coupons only to the top 5% with the highest scores. What action should the data analyst take FIRST?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Remove the post-cancellation record column, which cannot be known at prediction time, from the features and rebuild the features using only information available at prediction time

choices.label: B
choices.text: Replace the values in that column with the overall mean to reduce the skew in the distribution, and then retrain the model with the same feature set

choices.label: C
choices.text: Double the amount of training data to prevent overfitting and evaluate by increasing only the number of cross-validation folds while keeping the same column included

choices.label: D
choices.text: Give the column a large L2 regularization weight and adjust hyperparameters so that the model depends less on this column, and then train

explanation: Removing the post-cancellation record column that does not exist at prediction time is the correct answer. This column is a value generated after the correct answer (churn) has been determined, so it is target leakage, and it explains the gap between the 99% validation accuracy and the drop in production performance. Even if it is replaced with the mean, the problem that the source of the values is post-cancellation remains and information is still present. Increasing the amount of data or the number of folds will keep inflating the validation score as long as the leaked column remains. Regularization only reduces weights and does not eliminate the column, so the leakage remains.

prompt: An online retail marketing team wants to segment 200,000 customers by using 8 numeric features such as purchase frequency and amount. There are no labels, and the appropriate number of clusters is unknown. The team trained SageMaker K-Means for k=2 to 12 and recorded the within-cluster sum of squared distances for each k. The results will be used to design target groups for the next quarter's campaign, and the team has no statistics experts. Given the campaign budget, the number of target groups that can be managed is about 10 at most, and the number of clusters must allow marketers to describe the characteristics of each cluster. The customer features are already standardized and there are no missing values. Training takes a few minutes per k, and the final clustering model is trained one more time with the chosen k and used for the quarterly campaign. The point where the curve bends may not be clear, so the team wants to document its decision criteria. Which method MOST appropriately determines the number of clusters?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Select k=12, which gives the smallest within-cluster sum of squared distances, to split the clusters as finely as possible, and have people interpret each cluster later

choices.label: B
choices.text: Identify the elbow point, where the decrease in within-cluster sum of squared distances slows sharply as k increases, as a candidate, and finalize it based on how interpretable the clusters are

choices.label: C
choices.text: Compare the cluster numbers with the purchase label to choose the k with the highest validation accuracy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fix k at about 447, the square root of the number of data rows, to determine the number of clusters

explanation: K-Means is an unsupervised algorithm that groups similar observations without labels, so the number of clusters cannot be compared against a correct answer. Because the within-cluster sum of squared distances keeps decreasing as k increases, the common approach is to take the elbow point, where the decrease slows sharply, as a candidate and finalize it based on business interpretability. Looking only at the minimum sum of squared distances always favors larger k, which leads to meaningless segmentation. An accuracy criterion cannot be calculated because there are no labels. Fixing k at the square root of the number of rows has no basis and would split 200,000 customers into 447 clusters.

prompt: The marketing analytics team at a subscription service company performs K-means clustering for customer segmentation. The features are annual purchase amount (0 to 5,000,000 KRW), number of visits (0 to 30), and app rating (1 to 5). The results show that the clusters are effectively divided by purchase amount alone. None of the three features has missing values, outliers have already been handled, and the marketing team wants to compare the profile of each cluster and design tailored benefits that reflect all three features. There are 800,000 customers, and the number of clusters k=6 has already been agreed upon. The clustering results will be used in the next quarter's CRM campaign, so it must be possible to interpret the average profile of each cluster in the original units. The team has agreed not to change the K-means algorithm itself. The scaling method must be reused with the same values when scoring new customers after training. Which preprocessing is MOST appropriate to solve this problem?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Keep only the purchase amount column and remove the other features, simplifying the data so that the basis for the clusters becomes a single clear criterion

choices.label: B
choices.text: K-means is an algorithm that is not affected by the scale of features, so treat the current results as normal and skip preprocessing

choices.label: C
choices.text: Multiply the number of visits and the app rating by 100,000 so that they become similar in magnitude to the purchase amount, using arbitrary weights

choices.label: D
choices.text: Standardize all numeric features to a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1 so that each feature contributes to the distance calculation with a similar weight

explanation: Standardization is the correct answer. K-means uses Euclidean distance, so the purchase amount, with its large range of values, dominates the distance, and the other features hardly contribute to cluster formation. If you keep only the purchase amount, you deliberately discard the information in the other features. The claim that K-means is not affected by scale is the opposite of the facts. Multiplying by arbitrary constants is a weighting without basis, and because the units differ by feature, it is hard to reproduce.

prompt: A manufacturer's sensor analytics team collects about 600 correlated sensor values per machine, and the training data is 40 million rows. To reduce noise and shorten training time, the team wants to reduce the dimensionality by using the SageMaker built-in PCA algorithm. Each row is the measurement of one machine at a single point in time, and this job is used as an input preprocessing step for a later anomaly detection model. All of the sensor values are numeric and missing values have already been interpolated, and the preprocessing job must finish within two hours every night. Training runs on several ml.m5.4xlarge instances, and the number of dimensions to keep is set to the number at which the explained variance reaches 95% or more. The PCA model is saved so that the same transformation can be applied at inference time. Which PCA mode is MOST appropriate for this data, which has very many observations and very many features?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use randomized mode, which uses an approximation algorithm to efficiently handle data with many observations and many features

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use regular mode, because there is no difference between modes even for large-scale data, and perform the exact decomposition as is

choices.label: C
choices.text: PCA is a supervised learning algorithm, so create a label column and run it in classification mode to perform supervised dimensionality reduction

choices.label: D
choices.text: All features must be one-hot encoded before dimensionality reduction, so run it in regular mode after the encoding

explanation: Randomized mode is the correct answer. The documentation distinguishes between the two: regular is for sparse data with a moderate number of observations and features, and randomized is for data with a large number of both observations and features, using an approximation algorithm. 40 million rows and 600 features fall into the latter case. Regular mode does not suit this scale, and the claim that there is no difference between modes is also wrong. PCA is an unsupervised algorithm, so no labels are needed. The sensor values are already numeric, so one-hot encoding is not needed.

prompt: A financial MLOps team builds a retraining pipeline with SageMaker Pipelines. If the accuracy in the evaluation step is below 0.90, the model must not be registered in the registry, and a registered model must become a production deployment target only after a reviewer examines and approves it. The pipeline runs automatically every Monday on new data, and the approval history of the models must be kept for auditing. The team has limited the approvers to two people and does not want to introduce a new CI/CD tool. The evaluation report is stored in Amazon S3 as JSON, and the evaluation metrics are recorded together in the model package. The service operations team wants the deployment pipeline to pick up only approved versions. The approvers want to check the evaluation metrics and the model explainability material on a single screen. Select the two configurations that meet these requirements. (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Register the model as a new version in a model group in the Model Registry with the approval status left as pending manual approval, and deploy after approval

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn on pipeline step caching to reuse the results of the previous run so that evaluation is not repeated, and use it in place of the criteria check

choices.label: C
choices.text: Store all model versions in Amazon S3 in folders by date and have operators verbally decide which model to deploy by looking at the folder names

choices.label: D
choices.text: Compare the evaluation result property with a threshold in a condition step, and connect it so that the model registration step runs only when it passes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Add code in the training step that fails the job if accuracy is low, and automatically approve all registered models regardless of the results

explanation: The correct configurations are comparing the evaluation metric with a threshold in a condition step, and registering the model in the Model Registry in a pending manual approval state. The condition step prevents the subsequent registration step from running if the criterion is not met, and the registry manages model versions and approval status so that only approved models become deployment targets. Code that fails in the training step and automatic approval of everything violate the approval review requirement. Step caching only reduces repeated runs and is not a quality criteria check. S3 folders and verbal decisions make tracking and governance difficult.

prompt: A marketing analytics team calculated the Pearson correlation coefficient between advertising spend and sales and got 0.02, almost zero, so one analyst proposed excluding the advertising spend column from the model. However, the scatter plot clearly shows an inverted-U shape, in which sales are highest when advertising spend is in the middle range and low at both extremes. The data is monthly records from 3,000 stores, and missing values and outliers have already been cleaned up. The results of this analysis are used for allocating the marketing budget, so the variable selection decision directly affects the accuracy of sales forecasts. The model is a gradient boosting tree that predicts monthly sales per store, and in addition to advertising spend, there are 20 features such as store area, trade area, and season. If the advertising spend column is excluded, the budget simulation feature cannot be used. Which conclusion is MOST appropriate from a data interpretation perspective?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A correlation coefficient near 0 means that the two variables are independent, so treat the shape of the scatter plot as chance, exclude the advertising spend column, and retrain the model with only the remaining features

choices.label: B
choices.text: Standardizing the advertising spend raises the correlation coefficient, so standardize it and keep this column only if the correlation coefficient becomes sufficiently large

choices.label: C
choices.text: The shape of the scatter plot is due to outliers, so delete the values at both extremes, recalculate the correlation coefficient, and decide whether to keep it

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Pearson correlation coefficient measures only linear relationships, so a nonlinear relationship may exist; keep the column and use a nonlinear model or polynomial features

explanation: The Pearson correlation coefficient indicates only the strength of a linear relationship, so for a symmetric nonlinear relationship such as an inverted U, it can be close to 0. Therefore the column should be kept, and the relationship should be captured with a nonlinear model or polynomial features. A correlation of 0 does not mean independence. Standardization does not change the Pearson correlation coefficient. Deleting both extremes discards the information in the range where the relationship is clearest and amounts to manipulating the data to fit a conclusion.

prompt: The confusion matrix of a medical image screening model being introduced by a hospital's radiology department is TP 160, FP 40, FN 240, and TN 9,560. The medical staff consider missing a patient to be a much bigger problem than a false alarm, and a recall of 40% is unacceptable. Validation shows that the model's predicted probabilities are reasonably calibrated for whether a case is positive, and inference is provided through a real-time endpoint. Retraining would require more labeled images, which cannot be obtained this quarter. The threshold can be changed in the setting of the application that receives the call results, and the radiologists personally recheck every image flagged as positive. There are about 500 exams per day. Which action is MOST appropriate to increase recall without retraining the model, even if the precision of 80% is partly sacrificed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Raise the probability threshold for classifying a case as positive above 0.5 to make positive classification stricter, and also check whether the number of false alarms decreases

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower the probability threshold for classifying a case as positive below 0.5, and check the balance between recall and precision with the validation data

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the evaluation metric to accuracy and select the threshold at which accuracy is highest

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a post-processing rule that calibrates only the negative predictions in order to increase the number of TN

explanation: Precision is 160/(160+40)=0.8 and recall is 160/(160+240)=0.4. Lowering the threshold classifies more samples as positive, so FN decreases and recall rises, at the cost of increased FP and lower precision; this matches the requirement to prioritize recall without retraining, and the balance is checked with validation data. Raising the threshold lowers recall further. An accuracy criterion is pulled toward the majority class and does not reduce missed patients. Calibration that increases TN has nothing to do with missed patients.

prompt: A video analysis model at a media analytics company accepts videos of up to 600 MB per request and takes 10 to 20 minutes to process each one. Requests arrive only during business hours and not at all at night. Customer requests arrive with video files, several dozen at a time during business hours, and the results can be received a few minutes later or delivered through a separate notification. The model runs on one type of GPU instance, and there are only two operations staff. Result notifications are sent through Amazon SNS, and failed requests may be retried. Customers upload videos directly to Amazon S3, and the model container is already prepared to be compatible with SageMaker. The result files from one request are stored under a request ID prefix in Amazon S3. Which deployment method has the LEAST operational overhead while ensuring that no instance cost is incurred during idle time?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Run a real-time endpoint 24 hours a day, include the video directly in the request body and wait for the response synchronously, and extend the connection timeout limit in case processing takes longer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a serverless inference endpoint, set the memory to the maximum, and send the video file directly in the request body

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a SageMaker asynchronous inference endpoint and configure auto scaling to reduce the instance count to 0 when there are no requests

choices.label: D
choices.text: Put API Gateway in front of a real-time endpoint, split the video into pieces, divide it into multiple requests, and call them synchronously

explanation: An asynchronous inference endpoint with scaling in to 0 instances is the correct answer. Asynchronous inference queues requests through Amazon S3 for large payloads (up to 1 GB) and long processing times (up to 1 hour), and it saves cost by scaling in to 0 instances when there are no requests. Running a real-time endpoint continuously incurs cost even at night. Serverless has no idle cost, but 600 MB videos and 10 to 20 minutes of processing do not match its intended use. Splitting the video and calling synchronously adds splitting and reassembly logic and more operational burden.

prompt: A generative AI research team wants to train a transformer with about 13 billion parameters in Amazon SageMaker. The model does not fit into the memory of a single GPU, so with data parallel training an out-of-memory error occurs at the start. The training script is already written based on PyTorch FSDP, and the team wants to modify it as little as possible. The training environment is several ml.p4d.24xlarge instances. Given the research schedule, there is no time to rewrite the script with a new framework, and because one training run takes several days, GPU utilization is also important. Training uses 4 ml.p4d.24xlarge instances and reads data directly from Amazon S3. The team wants to use the training containers provided by SageMaker as is. Which approach MOST appropriately meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Split the model across multiple GPUs by using the sharded data parallelism and tensor parallelism features of the SageMaker model parallelism library (SMP v2)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase only the number of GPUs with the data parallelism library so that the batch is split across GPUs for processing

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the number of training instances and raise the overall batch size to increase throughput while keeping the configuration in which each instance holds an identical full copy of the model

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the input mode to Pipe to reduce the memory used for loading the training data

explanation: The model parallelism library is for splitting a large model that is hard to train because of the memory of a single GPU across multiple GPUs and nodes, and SMP v2 is designed to align with the PyTorch FSDP API so FSDP scripts can be brought over with minimal modification, and it provides hybrid sharded data parallelism and tensor parallelism. Data parallelism that only increases the number of GPUs does not split the model, so the single-GPU memory limit remains. The configuration that keeps replicas has the same limit, and Pipe mode only affects loading of input data and has nothing to do with model memory.

prompt: A SaaS company provides XGBoost demand forecasting models trained separately for each of 600 customers. All of the models use the same framework and container, and most models are invoked only a few times a day. When a new customer is added, the company wants to just add the model file without creating an endpoint. All customer models are retrained once a month and saved as new artifacts in Amazon S3, and each model is on the order of tens of megabytes. There is strong pressure to reduce cost and there are three operations staff. Each customer's training data must be stored separately, and the model artifacts are under customer prefixes. Which customer model to use is specified in the request at invocation. A delay of about a day before a new customer model takes effect is acceptable. Occasionally slow first invocations are acceptable. Which approach is the MOST cost-effective?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a single-model real-time endpoint on ml.m5.large for each customer so that the model is always loaded in memory

choices.label: B
choices.text: Include all 600 models in a single container image, increase the image size, and deploy it as a single-model endpoint

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deploy to a single multi-model endpoint, keeping the models in Amazon S3 so they are loaded dynamically when invoked

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a serverless endpoint for each customer and individually set the memory of each endpoint to match the model size

explanation: A multi-model endpoint is the correct answer. It serves many models of the same framework from shared containers and instances to improve utilization, and models are loaded and cached from Amazon S3 at invocation time, so no endpoint update is needed when a model is added. The slow first invocation of rarely used models is an acceptable condition stated in the question. Having a single-model endpoint per customer multiplies cost by 600, and including everything in the image makes updates difficult. Serverless endpoints per customer also require creating an endpoint per model, which increases the management burden when adding models.

prompt: A smart factory company ingests events sent by about 200,000 factory sensors into Kinesis Data Streams (provisioned mode, 8 shards). It currently uses the factory code (5 values) as the partition key, so writes are concentrated on only some shards and ProvisionedThroughputExceeded errors occur. Consumers need only a guarantee of event order per sensor and do not need a global order across all events. The sensor firmware cannot be changed, but the producer code on the ingestion side can be modified, and switching to on-demand mode is not being considered this time because of a cost approval issue. The producer sends events in batches with the PutRecords API, and the errors are concentrated for a few minutes right after shift changes. The consumer is AWS Lambda. Which actions appropriately resolve the errors? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase the stream retention period to 7 days to raise the per-second write limit that each shard can accept

choices.label: B
