choices.text: Leave the partition key as it is and increase the shards from 8 to 64 so that the 5 factory codes are spread across all shards

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use a random number as the partition key for each record to distribute the load while still preserving per-sensor ordering

choices.label: D
choices.text: If the write limit is still insufficient after the keys are distributed, split shards to increase the overall write throughput of the stream

choices.label: E
choices.text: Change the partition key to a high-cardinality value such as the sensor ID so that writes are distributed evenly across many shards

explanation: Kinesis maps a record to a single shard by the hash of the partition key, so if there are only 5 keys, then even if you add shards, the writes are concentrated on at most 5 shards; changing to a high-cardinality key such as the sensor ID distributes them. Because the same sensor goes to the same shard, per-sensor ordering is also preserved. If the per-shard write limit (1 MB per second or 1,000 records per second) is still insufficient after distribution, increase the shards to raise total throughput. A random key breaks per-sensor ordering, and the retention period has nothing to do with the write limit.

prompt: A customer support platform team trains a model that classifies 400,000 English customer inquiries into 12 categories by using SageMaker BlazingText in supervised mode. The data is currently stored as CSV in the form 'category,sentence', the sentences are raw text, and uppercase and lowercase letters and punctuation are mixed. There are about 30,000 records per class, and training runs on a single GPU instance. The transformation job can be run once with AWS Glue or Processing. At inference time as well, sentences preprocessed in the same way as in training must be sent. The training pipeline is built with Step Functions, so adding a preprocessing step at the front is not difficult. How should the input data be prepared for training to work correctly in the MOST appropriate way?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Upload a CSV with a header to the train channel as text/csv, and assume that the algorithm automatically skips the header row and reads the first column as the label

choices.label: B
choices.text: Leave the sentences as raw text and just add a prefix to the category, and BlazingText will tokenize the sentences automatically

choices.label: C
choices.text: Format each line as '__label__category token token ...', preprocess the sentences into space-separated tokens, and upload a single file to the train channel

choices.label: D
choices.text: Convert the sentences to JSON arrays, create the labels as a separate file, and upload it to the label channel

explanation: BlazingText expects a single text file preprocessed into space-separated tokens, and in supervised mode each line holds one sentence with a label that has the '__label__' prefix. So the category must be turned into a prefixed label and the sentences into tokenized form, and then uploaded to the train channel. The CSV format is not an input for this algorithm. The algorithm does not tokenize sentences automatically. There is no label-only channel, and the label must be included on each line.

prompt: A non-specialist analyst in the company wants to explore structured data in Amazon S3 and Amazon Athena without coding. The analyst wants to build, as a visual flow, a data quality report that checks for missing values and duplicates, target leakage analysis, and transformations such as categorical encoding, and to connect it to a later ML workflow. The analysis results must be reflected in a department dashboard every week, and the analyst has almost no programming experience other than SQL. The IT department cannot assign staff to operate a new server. The analyst's SageMaker domain and Canvas usage permissions have already been granted, and the analysis result data is stored in Amazon S3. Under the security policy, data must not leave the AWS account. The analyst prefers results that lead directly into the ML workflow rather than being downloaded as CSV. Which choice is MOST appropriate to minimize the operational burden?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Install Jupyter directly on Amazon EC2, implement all transformations and quality checks yourself with pandas scripts, operate it, and share the results as notebook files

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use the Data Wrangler data preparation flow and data insights features integrated into SageMaker Canvas

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stream the rows of the files with Kinesis Data Streams and check data quality by looking at real-time aggregation results

choices.label: D
choices.text: Send rows with suspected quality problems to a SageMaker Ground Truth labeling job so that people review them one by one

explanation: Data Wrangler integrated into Canvas is the correct answer. It lets you connect to Amazon S3 and Athena, and build and export a flow with data insights and quality reports, target leakage analysis, and transformations such as categorical encoding without coding. Building it directly on Amazon EC2 means operating servers and code, which creates a large operational burden. Kinesis streaming is not a data quality inspection tool for static data. Ground Truth is for labeling training data and is not used for quality checks.

prompt: A data platform team preprocesses 800 CSV files in Amazon S3 (400 GB in total) in a SageMaker Processing job on a single ml.m5.4xlarge, and it takes 6 hours. Each file is processed independently and the results are stored per file under an output prefix. The output file names must correspond one-to-one with the input file names. The preprocessing script is code shared with other teams, so changes must be minimized, and the job runs once a day with a goal of reducing the processing time to within 1 hour. Each input CSV is about 500 MB per file and there is no ordering dependency between files. The output is written to a different Amazon S3 prefix in the same Region, and the cost of one daily run should be at a similar level to what it is now. How should the job be configured so that each instance processes different files?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase the instance count to 8 and leave the input as FullyReplicated so that all instances download all the files and each outputs all of the results

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keep the instance count at 1 and change the input mode to Pipe to eliminate download time

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keep the instance count at 1 and switch to a larger instance type to increase the processing speed of a single node

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the instance count to 8 and specify ShardedByS3Key for the S3DataDistributionType of the input so that the files are divided among the instances

explanation: ShardedByS3Key divides the data by S3 object key and has each processing instance download one portion, so for this job, in which the files are independent, increasing the instances to 8 processes them in parallel without code changes. FullyReplicated replicates all of the data to every instance, so the same work is done 8 times and the time is not reduced. Pipe mode does not increase parallelism because there is only 1 instance. A larger instance does not match the requirement that each instance process different files.

prompt: In a real estate price prediction team's linear regression model, both the 'net floor area (m²)' and 'net floor area (pyeong)' columns are included as features, and their correlation coefficient is close to 1.0. Each time the model is retrained, the signs and magnitudes of the coefficients of the two columns fluctuate greatly, making interpretation impossible. The model already has sufficient predictive performance, but management has requested material explaining the price impact per unit of area, so coefficient interpretation is needed. There are 35 features in total, the model is retrained once a month, and the meaning of the remaining features must be preserved. The model is a scikit-learn linear regression in an internal notebook, and applying L2 regularization can be done in a single line of code. According to the data dictionary, one of the two columns is a derived column calculated from the other. Which action is MOST appropriate to stabilize the interpretation of the coefficients while maintaining predictive performance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Remove one of the two columns that carry duplicate information, or apply L2 regularization, to reduce the coefficient instability caused by multicollinearity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create and add a new interaction column by multiplying the values of the two columns so that the model learns the relationship between the two columns directly, and then re-estimate and interpret the coefficients

choices.label: C
choices.text: Randomly sample only half of the rows of the training data to weaken the correlation between the two columns, and then train the model

choices.label: D
choices.text: Apply a log transformation to both columns and keep them as they are, repeating training while watching whether the correlation coefficient becomes lower

explanation: Removing one column or using L2 regularization is the correct answer. The pyeong value is the m² value multiplied by a constant, so it is a complete duplicate, and this kind of multicollinearity makes the coefficients unstable. Adding an interaction column increases collinearity. Sampling rows does not weaken the correlation, because the linear relationship between the two columns is the same in every row. A log transformation only turns a constant multiple into a simple shift, so the two columns still have a perfect correlation.

prompt: A computer vision team at an autonomous driving parts company runs a PyTorch training job on an image dataset of about 6 TB in Amazon S3. The entire dataset does not fit in the training instance's local storage, and in File mode it takes a long time waiting for the download before starting. The training code opens and reads regular file paths, and code changes must be minimized, and the team does not want to configure separate storage such as FSx for Lustre. The team also wants to avoid changing the VPC network configuration. The dataset consists of hundreds of thousands of image files, and training runs on a single ml.p4d.24xlarge instance. The data loader has already been written to open images from a list of file paths. Which input method MOST appropriately meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Specify Pipe as the input mode and modify the training code to read the named pipe in order at every epoch

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keep File mode and enlarge the EBS volume of the training instance to be larger than the dataset, and then train after the download

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an FSx for Lustre file system, mount it together with the VPC configuration so that the training job reads from it, and synchronize the Amazon S3 data separately

choices.label: D
choices.text: Specify FastFile as the input mode and set the S3 prefix as the channel data source so that the required objects are read on demand

explanation: FastFile mode exposes S3 objects like a POSIX file system and streams them on demand at the moment the training script reads them, so there is no waiting for a full download, the dataset can be larger than local storage, and code that uses regular file paths can be left as is. Pipe mode requires changing the code to read the pipes in epoch order. File mode with an enlarged EBS volume still waits for the full download. FSx for Lustre requires VPC configuration and operating separate storage, which conflicts with the constraints.

prompt: For a regression model built by a logistics company's forecasting team, the training RMSE is 18.2 and the validation RMSE is 18.9, which are almost the same, but both are far from the business target of 8 or less. The learning curve flattens out early and the L2 regularization strength is set very high. The current model is a linear regression, there are 12 available features, and there are 800,000 training rows. Training time is not a concern, improving prediction accuracy is the priority, and no new labeled data can be obtained. The validation set has the same distribution as the training set, and apart from the bottom few, the feature importances are all meaningful values. Training finishes in a few minutes on a single ml.m5.2xlarge instance. Additional feature candidates can be derived from the existing 12 features. Which actions appropriately improve this situation? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add derived features such as interaction terms, or switch to a model with greater expressive power such as a deeper tree

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reduce the number of features in the training data to make the model simpler

choices.label: C
choices.text: Replicate the training rows from the same distribution 10 times to increase the number of samples, and retrain the same model

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lower the L2 regularization strength so that the model fits the training data better

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increase the dropout rate and reduce the early stopping patience so that training stops earlier

explanation: When both the training error and the validation error are high and similar, it is a sign of underfitting (high bias). In this case, you should reduce excessive regularization and increase capacity by adding derived features or switching to a more expressive model. Raising dropout or stopping earlier restricts the model further and makes underfitting worse. Reducing the number of features makes expressive power even lower. Replicating the same rows adds no information, so the training error does not improve and only the risk of overfitting increases.

prompt: A speech recognition service team is updating the model on a real-time endpoint and wants to avoid having a faulty model affect all traffic at once. The team wants to verify the model first with a small amount of traffic and move the rest if there are no problems, and if the error rate Amazon CloudWatch alarm fires, it must automatically roll back to the previous model. The endpoint handles an average of 150 requests per second, and the error rate of the currently running model is already monitored with CloudWatch. The deployment must proceed while the service is running, without a maintenance window, and the endpoint name must not change. The new model uses the same instance type as the existing one, and even if the deployment fails, serving of the previous model must be unaffected. The change to the endpoint configuration can be performed with the SageMaker deployment guardrails feature. Which configuration meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Shift traffic to the new fleet all at once with all-at-once traffic shifting, and if a problem occurs, have an operator manually restore the previous configuration from the console, judging by comparing the error rates before and after the deployment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delete the existing endpoint and then create a new model endpoint with the same name, completing the deployment after a short interruption

choices.label: C
choices.text: Update the endpoint by specifying canary traffic shifting for blue/green deployment guardrails, a baking period, and CloudWatch alarms for automatic rollback

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deploy the new model as a shadow variant so that user responses are still served by the existing model, and when promoting it, replace everything at once without alarms

explanation: Canary traffic shifting with an automatic rollback alarm is the correct answer. In the canary approach, a small portion of traffic is first sent to the new fleet and then the rest is shifted, and if the specified alarm fires during the baking period, all traffic returns to the previous fleet. All-at-once affects all traffic at once and relies on manual restoration. Deleting and recreating causes an interruption and offers no means of rollback. A shadow variant is for validation, and replacing everything at once on promotion does not meet the requirements for gradual shifting and automatic rollback.

prompt: A commerce recommendation team wants to validate response latency and prediction distribution with actual production traffic before deploying a new version of the recommendation model. The responses returned to users must continue to be the results of the existing model, and the results of the new model must not be exposed to users. The offline metrics of the new model were slightly higher than those of the existing model, but its latency under real traffic is not yet known. The new model will run on the same instance type as the existing one, and the validation is planned to continue for several days. The latency target for recommendation responses is a p99 of 200 ms. The responses of the shadow variant must be stored separately so they can be compared later with the results of the existing model. The new model and the existing model are different versions of the same container image. What is the SAFEST way to validate this on a single endpoint?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set both models as production variants with weights of 50:50 so that user requests are split half and half

choices.label: B
choices.text: Replace the endpoint with one containing only the new model so that it immediately handles all traffic, and roll back manually if a problem occurs

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the endpoint configuration, specify the existing model as the production variant and the new model as a shadow variant so that requests are duplicated and sent to it

choices.label: D
choices.text: Apply the new model to last month's logs as a batch transform job and compare the results, skipping validation with real-time traffic

explanation: A shadow variant is the correct answer. A shadow variant receives a copy of production traffic and is used to validate a new component over a long period, and the production variant continues to handle user responses, so the shadow results are not exposed to users. With 50:50 weights, half of the users receive the responses of the new model. Replacing the entire endpoint exposes all users to risk. A batch comparison using past logs does not meet the requirement to validate real-time latency and the current traffic distribution.

prompt: A team finished a SageMaker automatic model tuning job last week (100 training jobs, objective metric validation:auc). This time, newly collected data has been added, so the training data is different, and the team wants to tune again with narrowed hyperparameter ranges based on the previous results. The objective metric and the algorithm (XGBoost) are the same. This tuning can use at most 60 training jobs, and one tuning run takes several hours on CPU instances. The previous tuning job remains in the same account in a completed state, and the hyperparameter names and types are the same as last time. The new data is about 20% larger than before. The team wants to continue using the results of the previous job rather than discarding them. What is the MOST appropriate way to use the previous results to improve search efficiency?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Specify the previous tuning job as the parent and create a warm start job with WarmStartType set to TRANSFER_LEARNING

choices.label: B
choices.text: Specify the previous tuning job as the parent and create a warm start tuning job with WarmStartType set to IDENTICAL_DATA_AND_ALGORITHM

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fix the best hyperparameter values from the previous tuning job as static values and run a training job only once

choices.label: D
choices.text: Do not use the previous results, create a new tuning job from scratch with the new data, and increase the number of training jobs to 200

explanation: Warm start uses the results of previous tuning jobs in the search of the new job, and when the input data changes, you must use the TRANSFER_LEARNING type, which allows changes such as the input data and hyperparameter ranges. It also satisfies the constraints that the metric and the hyperparameter types be the same. IDENTICAL_DATA_AND_ALGORITHM assumes the same input data as the parent, so it does not fit this requirement, in which the data has changed. Fixing the best values and running once gives up the search, and starting over discards the existing results.

prompt: An ML platform team runs a training algorithm in SageMaker with its own Docker container (BYOC). In the CreateTrainingJob request, it passes learning_rate and epochs as hyperparameters and specifies two channels, train and validation, in File mode. The container image has already been pushed to Amazon ECR, and the training code uses a library shared with other internal services. The team does not want to hardcode S3 paths or channel names in the code. The training code was written directly without the SageMaker training toolkit, and when training finishes, the model must be saved to the designated path so that SageMaker can upload the model artifacts to Amazon S3. How should the training script in the container be implemented so that it reads these values and the data correctly?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hyperparameters are passed automatically as command-line arguments when the container starts, so read argv, read the data from the /data/train path, and assume that the data from the two channels is merged into one directory

choices.label: B
choices.text: No code to read hyperparameters is needed; hardcode the S3 URI in the script and download directly with boto3

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hyperparameters are passed as JSON under /opt/ml/model, and the data from the two channels is provided merged into one directory

choices.label: D
choices.text: Read the hyperparameters from the hyperparameters.json file (/opt/ml/input/config), and read each channel's data from the /opt/ml/input/data/channel_name directories

explanation: SageMaker provides the hyperparameters from CreateTrainingJob to the container as the file /opt/ml/input/config/hyperparameters.json (the values are strings), and in File mode it creates a /opt/ml/input/data/channel_name directory for each channel and places the data there. By default, the container is started with the train argument, and the hyperparameters do not arrive as command-line arguments. Hardcoding the S3 URI ignores the channel configuration. /opt/ml/model is the location where the resulting training artifacts are written, and the channels are not merged but provided separately.

prompt: A manufacturing company's quality team builds a model that classifies 12 defect types. There are only about 300 labeled images per type, and training from scratch causes the validation accuracy to plateau. The team uses SageMaker built-in algorithms, does not want to write neural network code directly, and also wants to reduce training time and GPU cost. Training uses a single GPU instance, and the resulting model will be deployed to edge devices on the company's quality inspection line. Marking the location of the defect is not needed, and only classifying the type is required. Compilation for edge deployment is handled in a separate step, so this question deals only with the training approach. 50 validation images per type have been set aside separately. The inference latency target on the edge device is within 100 ms per image. What is the MOST appropriate approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Train the built-in image classification algorithm from scratch with the default (use_pretrained_model=0), greatly increase the number of epochs, and train without data augmentation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Group the images into 12 clusters with K-Means and use the cluster numbers as is as the defect types

choices.label: C
choices.text: Set use_pretrained_model=1 in the built-in image classification algorithm to load pretrained weights and fine-tune with transfer learning

choices.label: D
choices.text: Switch to the object detection algorithm to train it to learn the location of defects in the image as well

explanation: The built-in image classification algorithm can be trained with transfer learning when there are not many labeled images, and with use_pretrained_model=1 it loads pretrained network weights and converges quickly even with little data, which reduces time and GPU cost without writing code. Training from scratch and only increasing epochs continues to cause overfitting and plateaus with small data. K-Means is unsupervised clustering, so there is no guarantee that cluster numbers match the defect types. Object detection requires location annotations and is unrelated to the requirements.

prompt: An advertising platform team predicts whether an ad will be clicked using sparse features of about 3 million dimensions, produced by one-hot encoding user ID, ad ID, placement, and device type. Interactions between pairs of features (for example, the combination of a particular ad category and a particular placement category) are important, and assigning a separate weight to each interaction would cause the number of parameters to explode. The training data is 500 million rows per day, and the team plans to perform both training and inference with the model on CPU instances. Sufficient click labels have been obtained, and the team wants to deliver this with a SageMaker built-in algorithm. Predictions are computed once a day in a batch and uploaded to the ad server. User IDs have millions of distinct values, but the team decided to use the one-hot sparse representation as is rather than embeddings or hashing. Which algorithm MOST appropriately meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use Linear Learner to learn linear weights for all features and leave it to the model to reflect the interactions implicitly

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use k-NN to predict by voting on the click outcomes of nearby neighbors in the 3-million-dimensional space

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use Factorization Machines to learn the pairwise feature interactions of high-dimensional sparse data as low-dimensional factors

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use K-Means to cluster users and use the average click rate of each cluster as the predicted value

explanation: Factorization Machines extend a linear model and are designed to capture second-order (pairwise) interactions between features in high-dimensional sparse data with few parameters through factorization, and click prediction and recommendation are the typical use cases. The training input is Float32 recordIO-protobuf, and CPU instances are recommended for sparse data. Linear Learner learns only linear terms and cannot reflect interactions. k-NN is inefficient for distance-based prediction in an extremely high-dimensional sparse space and does not learn interactions. K-Means is not supervised prediction.

prompt: A fintech company operates a fraud detection model. At payment authorization, the customer's recent transaction aggregate features must be read with a latency on the order of 10 milliseconds, and the model must also be periodically retrained using the past 2 years of history with the same feature definitions. The company also wants to reduce training-serving skew caused by differences between the feature computation code used for training and for serving. Model serving is done with a SageMaker real-time endpoint, and feature computation has so far been implemented separately by data engineers and data scientists. There are about 3 million payments per day, and staff to operate new infrastructure cannot be increased. The features are transaction aggregates over the last 1 hour, 24 hours, and 7 days, and are updated every time a new payment occurs. The data scientists and engineers want to write the same definition only once. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a SageMaker Feature Store feature group with both the online and offline stores turned on, and ingest with the same feature processing logic

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use only the offline store, query features with Athena for every payment request and use them in the authorization logic, fetching the query results anew each time without a cache

choices.label: C
choices.text: Store the training features as CSV in Amazon S3 and recompute the serving features separately in the application code

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use only the online store and do not keep historical data, so that retraining trains the model with only the latest values

explanation: A Feature Store feature group with both the online and offline stores turned on is the correct answer. The online store is for real-time prediction, reading the latest record with millisecond latency, and the offline store keeps all of the history for use in training and batch inference. Because ingestion uses the same processing logic, training-serving skew is also reduced. The offline store and Athena are for exploration and training, so they do not meet the authorization latency requirement. Recomputing with separate code leaves the skew, and using only the online store leaves no 2-year history.

prompt: A SaaS company's data engineering team has been accumulating 3 years of service logs in Amazon S3 with a year=/month=/day=/region= structure, and a new date partition is created every day. As the partitions have grown to tens of thousands, the planning phase of Athena queries has become slow, and the cost and delay of running a crawler every day to register new partitions are also a problem. The dates are continuous, and the regions are fixed at six. Most queries filter on the most recent month and a specific region, and all lookups are done only through Athena. Objects in past partitions do not change, and there is no possibility that new regions will be added. Several hundred cost reporting queries run every day, and the team does not want to change the Athena workgroup settings. Which method reduces query latency and operational burden the MOST?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure partition projection in the AWS Glue table properties, specifying the date range and the list of regions so that partition values are computed

choices.label: B
choices.text: Shorten the crawler schedule so that it runs every hour to reduce the delay in registering new partitions

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove all partition columns and store the entire log under one prefix to eliminate partition metadata lookups, and filter queries only by date conditions

choices.label: D
choices.text: Split the daily partitions into smaller hourly partitions to reduce the amount of data that queries read

explanation: With partition projection, Athena computes the partition values and locations directly from the date range and region list specified in the table properties, so no AWS Glue catalog lookup is needed, queries become faster, and there is no need to register new partitions manually. Shortening the crawler interval only increases cost and calls. Removing partitions makes every query scan everything. Hourly splitting increases the number of partitions further and increases the metadata burden. Note that projection applies only when querying through Athena.

prompt: An insurance company's fraud investigation team trains a binary classification model for insurance fraud detection with SageMaker Linear Learner. Because of limited reviewer capacity, at least 90% of alerts must be actual fraud, and within that constraint the model must catch as much fraud as possible. The fraud rate is about 1% of the total, and in past validation the balance between precision and recall differed greatly from one candidate model to another. The candidate models are several produced by hyperparameter tuning, and each training run takes a few minutes. The validation set contains enough fraud cases to calculate precision and recall stably. The team does not want to adjust the threshold separately on the calling side and wants to reflect this goal at the model selection stage. Which setting most directly reflects this goal when choosing one of several candidate models with the validation data?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set binary_classifier_model_selection_criteria to precision_at_target_recall and set target_recall to 0.9 to maximize precision

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set binary_classifier_model_selection_criteria to recall_at_target_precision and set target_precision to 0.9

choices.label: C
choices.text: Set binary_classifier_model_selection_criteria to accuracy and select the model with the highest validation accuracy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change loss to hinge_loss, interpret the output score as a probability, and determine the threshold at the 90% precision point

explanation: recall_at_target_precision selects the model that maximizes recall while keeping precision at the target_precision value, which matches the goal that 90% of alerts must be actual fraud and that as much as possible must be caught within that constraint. Conversely, precision_at_target_recall fixes recall and maximizes precision, so the direction is reversed. The default, accuracy, cannot reflect the precision constraint on imbalanced data. hinge_loss corresponds to support vector classification, so the score cannot be interpreted as a probability.

prompt: A bank's data team stores financial data in Amazon S3 with SSE-KMS encryption using a customer managed KMS key, and audits key usage with AWS CloudTrail. Even though the execution role of the SageMaker training job already has s3:GetObject permission on the bucket, the job fails with AccessDenied at the data download step. The same key and bucket are not shared with other departments' accounts and are within the same account. The encryption and key auditing requirements must be maintained, and permissions must be granted at the minimum level. The download error message contains KMS-related AccessDenied wording. The training data is updated once a month, and this execution role is used only for that training purpose. CloudTrail records show denied key usage events for the role. What is the MOST appropriate solution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the default encryption of the bucket to SSE-S3 so that objects can be read without calling KMS

choices.label: B
choices.text: Allow s3:* and kms:* permissions on all resources for the execution role to eliminate permission problems all at once, and do not change the key policy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn on bucket versioning to prevent the access denied error that occurs when objects are read

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add kms:Decrypt permission for that KMS key to the execution role policy and also allow that role in the key policy

explanation: To read an SSE-KMS object, the caller needs not only S3 read permission but also decrypt permission on the KMS key, so allowing only kms:Decrypt on that key in both the execution role policy and the key policy is the least-privilege solution. Changing to SSE-S3 gives up the requirement for auditing based on a customer managed key. Granting s3:* and kms:* on all resources violates the principle of least privilege. Versioning has nothing to do with read permission or decryption.

prompt: A price prediction team at a real estate information company uses linear regression. The area and price columns are skewed with a long right tail (a small number of ultra-high-priced homes exist), and the residuals grow larger as the price increases. The ultra-high-priced homes are real, normal data and cannot be deleted. The current mean absolute error is large and the error grows for higher-priced homes, and the model must remain a linear regression for interpretability. The training data is 120,000 records and missing value handling is already finished. The model coefficients can still be explained to the sales team as percentage changes after a log transformation. Predictions are converted back to the original units at the serving stage. Prediction error is evaluated on a relative error basis for higher-priced homes. Which transformation MOST appropriately mitigates this problem without discarding data?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply a log transformation to the price (and to the area if necessary) to reduce the skew in the distribution and the unevenness of the variance, and then train the model

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delete the rows for the ultra-high-priced homes in the top 5% to cut off the long tail of the distribution, and then train on the remaining data

choices.label: C
choices.text: Apply min-max normalization to all numeric columns to fit the range of values between 0 and 1, and then train with the same model

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bin the price column into intervals, one-hot encode it, and change the problem to a classification model designed to predict only the probability of each interval

explanation: A log transformation is the correct answer. It mitigates the right-skewed distribution and the variance that grows as values get larger, while keeping all rows. Deleting the ultra-high-priced rows violates the constraint that they cannot be deleted. Min-max normalization only changes the range and leaves the shape of the distribution and the heteroscedasticity as they are. Binning the price and converting to classification changes the regression objective itself, which loses information and also differs from the requirements.

prompt: A financial company must place the inference endpoint of a credit review assistance model inside a VPC in a private subnet, and under regulations must store all requests and responses in Amazon S3 with data capture. Callers must receive synchronous responses, and traffic is moderate during the day and almost none at night. Normal traffic is on the order of hundreds of requests per hour, and the security team has required that endpoint access be restricted to the internal network and AWS PrivateLink. The model can run inference on CPU, and the operations team also wants to reduce cost. The inference code runs in a container that uses an internal certificate, and the payload of one request is a few KB. The data capture logs are reviewed by the audit team every quarter. Even after the model is deployed, the change history of the network and data capture settings is subject to audit. Which deployment method is MOST appropriate to meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Turn on data capture for an instance-based real-time endpoint with VpcConfig specified, and adjust capacity with auto scaling

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure both the VPC configuration and data capture on a serverless inference endpoint to eliminate instance cost during idle time

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deploy as serverless first, then add the VPC configuration and data capture later from the console during operation, and restrict invocation with IAM policies until then

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scale the instance count of an asynchronous endpoint down to 0 and keep only the input and output S3 paths without a data capture configuration

explanation: A real-time endpoint with a VPC configuration and data capture specified is the correct answer. Serverless inference has VPC configuration and data capture on its list of unsupported features, so it cannot satisfy both requirements, and adding them later is impossible for the same reason. An instance-based endpoint can reduce cost for night traffic through auto scaling. An asynchronous endpoint does not meet the synchronous response requirement and does not use data capture, so it violates the requirements.

prompt: A cloud operations team collects 14 numeric metrics, such as CPU, memory, and disk I/O, from each server at 1-minute intervals. There are almost no failure labels, and the team wants to score data points that deviate from normal patterns and raise alerts based on a threshold. There are about 3,000 servers, and the training data is stored as CSV files in Amazon S3. With few model development staff, the team cannot design a neural network architecture by hand, and the threshold must be adjustable to reduce alert fatigue for on-call staff. Alarms are sent to the on-call tool, and the threshold is readjusted weekly by looking at the anomaly score distribution. The metrics CSV includes server ID and timestamp columns. Which is the MOST appropriate choice to meet these requirements with a SageMaker built-in algorithm and no labeling cost?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Train a Linear Learner binary classifier on whether a failure occurred, with labels filled in gradually by people, and make servers with a high predicted probability the alert targets

choices.label: B
choices.text: Forecast the metrics with DeepAR and treat actual values that fall outside the prediction interval as anomalies

choices.label: C
choices.text: Train an XGBoost binary classifier and collect labels for the times when failures occurred afterward to reflect them next quarter

choices.label: D
choices.text: Train Random Cut Forest and make the points where the anomaly score deviates from the mean by three or more standard deviations the alert targets

explanation: Random Cut Forest is an unsupervised anomaly detection algorithm designed to handle input of arbitrary dimension, so it assigns an anomaly score to each data point while looking at all 14 metrics together, and it is common to treat scores that deviate from the mean by three or more standard deviations as anomalies, which meets the alert threshold requirement without labels. Linear Learner and XGBoost classification can be trained only if failure labels exist. DeepAR is a time series forecasting algorithm whose purpose is to forecast metrics, and it does not directly produce an anomaly score that looks at the 14 metrics together, so its design purpose is different.

prompt: A content analytics team at a media company trains a topic model that discovers topics without labels from 30 million English articles, using a SageMaker built-in algorithm. The LDA job takes several days on a single CPU instance, so the training time must be reduced by parallelizing across multiple GPU instances. The corpus is already prepared in Amazon S3 as a word count matrix, the number of topics is set to 50, and training must finish within a day. The editorial team looks at the representative words of each topic to name them, so the per-document topic distribution must be obtainable. Because there is a training cost limit, the team prefers fewer instances if they finish in the same time. The resulting model is also used to classify each document into its highest-weighted topic. Which is the MOST appropriate choice to meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase the instance count of the LDA training job and train in a distributed manner on multiple CPU instances

choices.label: B
choices.text: Train BlazingText in supervised mode on multiple CPU instances to classify the articles by topic

choices.label: C
choices.text: Train word embeddings with BlazingText Word2Vec, and the topics of the documents are labeled automatically

choices.label: D
choices.text: Train a Neural Topic Model (NTM) in parallel on multiple GPU instances

explanation: NTM runs on both CPU and GPU and can be parallelized across multiple GPU instances, so it scales well to topic modeling of a large corpus. LDA supports only single-instance CPU training, so increasing the instance count does not distribute it. BlazingText in supervised mode is for classifying labeled text and does not support training on multiple CPU instances either. Word2Vec only creates word embeddings and does not produce a topic distribution for documents.

prompt: An advertising platform ingests about 8,000 JSON click events per second with Kinesis Data Streams. The analytics team wants to store these events in Amazon S3 as Parquet to reduce Athena scan cost, and does not want to operate its own compute infrastructure for the conversion. The event schema is already finalized and there are two data engineers. The results are used for daily reporting, so second-level real-time delivery is not needed. The result files accumulate under hourly S3 prefixes and are queried through an Athena table with the same schema. The schema changes once a quarter or less. Which combination of actions should be taken to meet the requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Define a table in the AWS Glue Data Catalog that matches the event schema and use it as the basis for the conversion schema

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn on record format conversion in the Firehose delivery stream and specify a JSON deserializer and a Parquet serializer

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deploy an EC2 consumer application that reads the stream, converts each record to a Parquet file, and uploads it to Amazon S3

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run an AWS Glue crawler on the Firehose output path, and the JSON objects are automatically converted to Parquet files

choices.label: E
choices.text: Specify GZIP as the S3 compression format of the Firehose delivery stream, and the JSON records are changed to Parquet format

explanation: Firehose converts JSON to Parquet by referring to the schema defined in the Glue Data Catalog, so combining the schema table definition and the record format conversion settings (JSON deserializer and Parquet serializer) meets the requirements without operating servers. A crawler only registers a table in the catalog and does not change the object format. Running your own EC2 consumer creates a server operations burden and many small files. A GZIP compression setting only reduces file size and does not change the format to columnar.

prompt: A payment anomaly detection team wants to apply a new model to only 10% of the total traffic on an endpoint first for comparison, and if the metrics are good, to increase the share without recreating or updating the endpoint. Latency and invocation counts per variant are checked in Amazon CloudWatch. The new model has finished offline evaluation, and the business team wants to compare metrics such as conversion rate between the two models over several weeks. The invoking code is shared by several services and is hard to modify. The share adjustment is performed by an operator through the CLI, and the conversion rate metric is aggregated from the invocation logs, distinguished by variant name. The new model starts with one instance of the same instance type. The two models use the same instance type, and the variant configuration does not change during the comparison period. What is the SIMPLEST way to meet this requirement without modifying the invoking code?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Implement the invoking code so that it chooses the new endpoint name with 10% probability, redeploy the application each time the share changes, and collect the metrics of the two endpoints separately

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create two variants and specify TargetVariant on all invocations so that the application directly controls the ratio at which it selects variants

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a separate endpoint for the new model and configure the traffic share to be adjusted by using target group weights on a load balancer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Specify weights of 9:1 on two production variants and then adjust the weights later with UpdateEndpointWeightsAndCapacities

explanation: Production variant weights and UpdateEndpointWeightsAndCapacities are the correct answer. Invocations are distributed according to the weight ratio, this API lets you change the share without updating the endpoint, and metrics per variant can be checked in CloudWatch. Choosing in the invoking code and specifying TargetVariant on every invocation both violate the constraint that the invoking code cannot be modified. Using a separate endpoint and a load balancer adds components and is not the simplest method.

prompt: A manufacturing company wants to move a transaction table from an on-premises PostgreSQL database (about 3 TB) to an Amazon S3 data lake for ML training. It must first load everything and then keep reflecting inserts, updates, and deletes that occur at the source into Amazon S3 within a few minutes. The source service cannot be interrupted, and Parquet format is preferred for analytical query efficiency. On-premises and AWS are connected with AWS Direct Connect, and the data team has no capacity to develop or operate a CDC tool itself. The source PostgreSQL is a version that supports logical replication, and a read-only account is ready. Deleted rows must also be distinguishable in the lake. The read load on the source database must stay within an acceptable range even during the initial load. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure an AWS DMS task with full load and ongoing change data capture (CDC), and specify Parquet as the format of the S3 target endpoint

choices.label: B
choices.text: Move the 3 TB first with AWS Snowball Edge, reflect subsequent changes to Amazon S3 by periodically bringing the device back in, and pause changes at the source while the device is being brought in

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dump the entire table every night with an AWS Glue JDBC job, overwrite the S3 partitions, and reflect changes the next day

choices.label: D
choices.text: Connect the query results of the source database directly to a Firehose delivery stream to write changed rows to Amazon S3 as Parquet

explanation: DMS supports both full load and CDC with Amazon S3 as a target, and the output format can be specified as Parquet, so it meets the requirement to continuously reflect changes without interrupting the source as a managed service. Snowball Edge is for one-time bulk transfers and cannot reflect changes within minutes. A nightly full dump has a one-day reflection delay and is disadvantageous for handling deletions and for cost. Firehose is not a source that reads the change logs of a database, so it cannot be used for this purpose.

prompt: A fintech company trains a binary classification model with the SageMaker built-in XGBoost on 40 million transaction rows in which about 2% are fraud (positive). With default settings, the model predicts almost all transactions as normal, so recall is low, and because fraud samples are valuable, the company does not want preprocessing that discards or duplicates data. Evaluation uses PR AUC. The training data is stored in Amazon S3, and the training job runs once a day. Only hyperparameters can be changed, and the structure of the training pipeline is kept. The positive ratio of the validation set is the same as that of the training set, and the team compares models by the ranking quality of the probability scores without adjusting the threshold. The resulting model is used for batch scoring every morning. Which action MOST appropriately meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set scale_pos_weight to about 0.02 to match the positive ratio, reducing the weight of positive examples

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set scale_pos_weight to about 49, the ratio of the number of negatives to the number of positives, and compare models by validation PR AUC

choices.label: C
choices.text: Randomly remove negative samples to reduce the training data to a 1:1 ratio with positives, and train

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep eval_metric at the default error and only greatly increase num_round to train for longer, without separately adjusting class weights

explanation: XGBoost's scale_pos_weight adjusts the balance between positive and negative weights for imbalanced classes, and the number of negatives divided by the number of positives is the typical setting. With 2% positives, negatives are 98%, so the value is about 49, and this also respects the constraint of not discarding or duplicating data. 0.02 is in the opposite direction and actually reduces the weight of positives. Undersampling by removing negatives violates the requirement not to discard data. The error metric and increasing rounds alone do not resolve the bias toward the majority class.

prompt: A logistics company needs a model that finds multiple pallets and forklifts per image from warehouse CCTV images and outputs the location (rectangle), type, and confidence of each object. The training data is JSON in which rectangle coordinates and classes are annotated for each image, and there is no plan to create pixel-level masks. The image resolution is 1920x1080, and about 50,000 new images arrive per day. Safety staff use the results for counting objects and proximity alerts, and the team has no staff who can design a neural network architecture. Training runs on a single ml.p3.2xlarge instance, and inference may be processed in a daily batch. There are three classes, pallet, forklift, and person, and there are on average 8 objects per image. Which SageMaker built-in algorithm is MOST appropriate to meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use Semantic Segmentation to classify every pixel of the image into a class to obtain the object regions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use Object Detection (SSD-based) to train on the rectangle annotations and output the location, class, and confidence of each object

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use the multi-label mode of Image Classification to output the names of all objects present in the image

choices.label: D
choices.text: Train Image Classification with a single label to output the single most likely class per image, and estimate the locations with post-processing

explanation: Object Detection uses the SSD framework to find all object instances in an image and outputs the rectangle location, class, and confidence, and it is trained on JSON annotations that contain rectangle coordinates and classes, so it matches the requirements exactly. Semantic Segmentation requires pixel-level mask annotations, which there is no plan to create, and it does not directly provide bounding boxes of instance locations. Image classification, whether multi-label or single-label, cannot output locations.

prompt: A financial company's fraud detection team creates derived features in SageMaker Processing during training and recomputes the same features with separate application code during real-time inference, so mismatches between training and serving values keep recurring. Inference must look up the latest features within tens of milliseconds per request, while training must read a large volume of feature history from past points in time. Two teams implement the same features separately, so the maintenance burden is also high. There are about 40 feature definitions, and new history is reflected once a day. The inference service runs on a SageMaker endpoint, and its execution role can read the feature store. All feature values are numeric, and online lookups need only the latest values. Which configuration MOST appropriately eliminates the duplication of feature computation logic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Load the training features into Amazon S3 and the inference features into Amazon DynamoDB through separate pipelines, maintain two copies of the transformation code, and periodically reconcile the values in the two stores manually

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a Feature Store feature group with both the online and offline stores turned on, ingest once, and use online lookups for inference and offline queries for training

choices.label: C
choices.text: Query the source data in Amazon S3 with Athena for every inference request to compute the latest features on the fly

choices.label: D
choices.text: Store all features in Amazon ElastiCache and read even the past history from the cache during training

explanation: A Feature Store feature group keeps features that were ingested once in both an online store for latest value lookups and an offline store that accumulates history in Amazon S3 (Parquet), so training reads the offline store with Athena or similar tools and inference looks up the online store with low latency, eliminating duplicated logic and value mismatches. Keeping two pipelines leaves the same mismatches to recur. An Athena query for every request cannot meet a latency of tens of milliseconds. ElastiCache is not suited to bulk reads of past history or to constructing point-in-time training data.

prompt: A computer vision team runs a training job that takes about 20 hours on GPU instances three times a week. The team wants to reduce cost, and the training gives the same result even if it is interrupted and resumed. It is acceptable for the job to wait if there is no Spot capacity. The job runs as a SageMaker training job, and the training script has already been written so that it can save the model state at every epoch. The training results are used at the meeting the next morning, so waiting up to two days is acceptable. The script is set up to write checkpoints to the local checkpoint path of the training container. The training job runs on a single instance and does not use distributed training. Training cost is aggregated monthly and reported to the finance team. Which configuration is MOST appropriate to reduce cost without losing progress when interrupted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Turn on managed Spot training, store checkpoints in Amazon S3, and set MaxWaitTimeInSeconds greater than MaxRuntimeInSeconds

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn on managed Spot training without checkpoints and set MaxWaitTimeInSeconds and MaxRuntimeInSeconds to the same value

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn on managed Spot training and have SageMaker automatically switch to an On-Demand instance and continue training if Spot capacity is lacking, with checkpoints stored only on the local disk

choices.label: D
choices.text: Train on On-Demand instances, but launch EC2 Spot Instances yourself and run the job while manually moving the checkpoint files

explanation: Managed Spot training with checkpoints and a MaxWait greater than MaxRuntime is the correct answer. If interrupted, SageMaker restores the checkpoint from Amazon S3 and resumes from the last point, and MaxWait must be greater than MaxRuntime to allow waiting for Spot capacity. If the two values are made equal without checkpoints, an interruption means starting over or there is no wait time. Managed Spot does not switch automatically to On-Demand; it waits and then stops. Managing Spot yourself only adds operational burden.

prompt: A team is building a card payment anomaly detection model. Normal transactions are 99.5% and fraudulent transactions are 0.5%, and the cost of missing fraud is much greater than the cost of a false positive. The team evaluated the model by accuracy, but classifying every transaction as normal also gave 99.5%. The model evaluates payment requests at hundreds per second, and suspected fraud transactions are reviewed manually by analysts, so the reviewers' workload must also be considered. The training data is 10 million records and XGBoost is used. The classification threshold must be adjusted to the analysts' daily review throughput (about 2,000 cases). The payment data has already been cleaned, and the training and validation split is by time order. The team intends to address the class imbalance through hyperparameters and changes to the evaluation method. Select the two actions that should be applied first to handle the imbalance correctly. (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Remove features with high variance from the normal transaction column so that the distribution difference between the two classes is reduced

choices.label: B
choices.text: Balance the entire dataset first with SMOTE, and then split into training and test sets to proceed with evaluation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduce the normal transactions in the test set to a 1:1 ratio and then continue to use accuracy as the main metric

choices.label: D
choices.text: Evaluate the model and the classification threshold based on the area under the precision-recall curve and recall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Adjust XGBoost's scale_pos_weight to give a greater weight to errors on the fraud class when training

explanation: The correct answers are giving weight to minority class errors with scale_pos_weight and evaluating by the area under the precision-recall curve and recall. The weight keeps training from ignoring fraud transactions, and since accuracy is meaningless under imbalance, a metric that is sensitive to the minority class is needed. If SMOTE is applied before the split, synthetic samples leak into the test set and inflate the evaluation. Reducing the test set to 1:1 distorts the real distribution, and accuracy is still an inappropriate metric. Removing high-variance features has nothing to do with imbalance.

prompt: An advertising data team converts JSON files that accumulate at several thousand per day under the raw/ prefix in Amazon S3 once a day with an AWS Glue Spark ETL job. Currently, every run reads all of the files again, and the run time keeps growing. The files accumulate under a single prefix with no date partitions, and objects that have already been processed are not modified. The job is a Glue 4.0 Spark job and the file format is JSON. The data ingestion structure is owned by another team and cannot be changed, and changes to the script must be minimized. The Glue job runs with 10 G.1X workers and writes its output as Parquet by date. On a day when the job fails, rerunning it with the same input must give the same result. What is the MOST appropriate way to process only the newly arrived objects?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Leave the job bookmark in the Pause state and manually specify the range of run IDs to process on each run

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run a crawler every day to register only new partitions in the catalog on the assumption that the job then reads only new data, leaving the bookmark disabled, adding no state-saving code, and leaving the read statements unchanged

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add a Lambda function that deletes objects after they are processed, and invoke a new job for each object through S3 events

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable the job bookmark, and save the processing state by calling job.init and job.commit in the script and specifying transformation_ctx in the read statements

explanation: When the AWS Glue job bookmark is turned on, it saves the state processed in previous runs so that the next run processes only new data. The state is loaded with job.init and saved at job.commit, and it is managed per transformation_ctx attached to the read statements, so this value must be specified; the S3 source identifies new objects by object modification time, and JSON is a supported format. The pause option does not update the state, and the range must be managed manually, which creates a large operational burden. This data has no partitions, so running a crawler does not reduce the range that is read. Deleting objects and invoking a job per object is a large change to the entire pipeline and does not fit the requirement to minimize script changes.
